candidates.exact_span: The percent solids of sewage sludge that contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 90% based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Alternative 8 applies—and thus whether the 90% solids threshold governs a reported measurement—depends on how 'unstabilized solids,' 'primary wastewater treatment process,' and 'prior to mixing with other materials' are interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or an anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of what counts as aerobic or anaerobic treatment change whether sludge is classified as containing unstabilized solids, which determines applicability of the 90% solids limit.

candidates.exact_span: When cover is placed on an active surface disposal site, the methane gas concentration in the air in any structure shall not exceed 25% of the lower ex plosive limit (LEL) for methane gas during the period that the disposal site is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when cover is placed, which structures qualify, and when the disposal site is 'active' changes whether the 25%-of-LEL limit applies, whether continuous structure methane monitoring is in scope, and how missing or non-numeric methane evidence is classified.

candidates.exact_span: The concentration of methane gas in air at the property line of the surface disposal site shall not exceed the LEL for methane gas during the period that the disposal site is active.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the property-line methane limit is operative turns on how 'property line,' 'LEL,' and 'during the period that the disposal site is active' are read; that in turn affects limit comparison, continuous monitoring obligation, and missing-evidence handling for property-line methane.

candidates.exact_span: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) Test - Once/Permit Life, performed within one year from the effective date of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TCLP monitoring was required in FY2025 depends on permit effective date and how 'Once/Permit Life' and the one-year window are counted; absent or late TCLP results are classified differently depending on that applicability.

Annual PCB monitoring frequency establishes the expected monitoring cadence; different readings of the annual obligation change whether missing PCB data reflects a required-but-unreported case or a non-applicable period.

candidates.exact_span: Methane Gas in covered structures on site - Continuous
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether continuous structure methane monitoring is required hinges on when structures are 'covered' and on site; that affects obligation rows and how gaps in continuous methane records are categorized.

candidates.exact_span: Methane Gas at property line - Continuous
candidates.computation_change_reason: Continuous property-line methane monitoring is tied to active surface disposal; interpretation of site activity and property-line scope changes whether monitoring was required and how missing continuous data is treated.
